description.value: The study examined gray-matter volume differences associated with cigarette smoking and methamphetamine dependence, and longitudinal gray-matter changes during early methamphetamine abstinence.

spans.text: This study aimed to separate effects of cigarette smoking from those of MA abuse on gray-matter volume.

value: we hypothesized that MA-dependent and control participants who smoke cigarettes would exhibit lower gray-matter volume in prefrontal, cingulate and insular cortices compared with Control Nonsmokers.

we therefore hypothesized that in striatum and globus pallidus, the MA-dependent sample would differ from two control groups that did not abuse MA, but that the two control groups would not differ from one another.
anticipating that gray matter would increase within regions where the early abstinent, MA-dependent participants had smaller gray-matter volumes than Control Smokers.
